answer: Independence beats headcount. A submission is paid only when three reviewers who share no prior transactions with the author agree on it, and that sample is redrawn every round. A farm can spin up a thousand clones, but it cannot make them strangers: they collapse into one dense cluster of mutual history. Honest reviewers arrive by separate paths, so their verdicts act as a beacon for real work. No fable about crowd size survives that check; the pigment of reputation only sticks to identities that outsiders actually inspected.
